detailed_rationale:
Le Travenues Technology (ixigo) is India's second-largest technology-driven online travel platform, covering trains, flights, buses and hotels through the ixigo, Confirmtkt and abhibus brands, serving a large user base (~480 million reported annual active users) via proprietary trip-planning/utility tools. FY26 revenue grew strongly to ~₹1,225-1,230cr from ~₹914cr in FY25 (~34% YoY, matching this universe's 3-year and 1-year revenue-growth figures of ~35% and ~34% respectively), but profit grew more slowly (~₹60cr to ~₹71-72cr, roughly +18-20%), implying margin compression — quarterly OPM has ranged from a strong ~8% down to a negative ~-2% (Sep-2025), showing real volatility rather than a clean scaling curve.
A specific earnings-quality flag from the one-off hunt: a meaningful share of reported profit appears to come from 'other income' (~₹44.5cr against full-year PAT of ~₹71cr) — consistent with interest income earned on cash raised in ixigo's 2024 IPO sitting in deposits, not from the core travel-booking operations. That means true operating profitability is materially lower than the headline PAT suggests, and as IPO cash gets deployed into growth capex/marketing or is simply drawn down over time, this profit tailwind should fade — a real consideration when judging whether current profit growth is sustainable.
Returns on capital are weak for the valuation: ROE ~6-9% and ROCE ~7% (and even weaker if 'other income' is stripped out) against a rich ~118x trailing P/E and ~4.3x book value. Working-capital days have deteriorated sharply (from ~18 to ~102 days), an unusual move for an OTA-model business that should typically run on favorable (low or negative) working capital by collecting from customers ahead of paying suppliers/airlines/railways — worth flagging as a genuine item to watch rather than dismissing as noise. The revenue growth itself is real and reflects genuine user/transaction scaling in a large addressable market (Indian travel bookings shifting online), but the profitability conversion, working-capital trend, and reliance on non-operating income are all real quality caveats behind the growth headline.
recommendation_rationale: Quant recommendation is Hold on both windows (final_score_3y ~47.0, final_score_1y ~48.7), driven by very high growth scores (~89/87) offset by a weak value score (~26) reflecting the rich multiple. I agree with Hold: the user/transaction growth is genuine, but weak ROE, margin volatility, deteriorating working capital, and a meaningful non-operating contribution to profit are real quality caveats that keep this from being a stronger call, without being negative enough (no balance-sheet distress, genuine revenue scale) to argue for a Sell even if the framework allowed one.
summary: ixigo (Le Travenues Technology) is a fast-growing Indian online travel platform with a large user base and strong revenue growth, but profit has grown more slowly than revenue, working-capital days have deteriorated notably, and a meaningful share of reported profit looks to come from interest income on IPO cash rather than core travel-booking operations. Returns on capital remain low (mid-single-digit ROE) against a rich ~118x earnings multiple. We rate this a Hold: genuine growth, but profitability quality and valuation both warrant caution.
positive_para: Genuine, strong revenue growth (~34% YoY) in a large, structurally under-penetrated online-travel market, with a sizeable user base (~480 million reported annual active users) across trains, flights, buses and hotels, and a nearly debt-free balance sheet giving it flexibility to keep investing in growth.
negative_para: Profit has grown materially slower than revenue, with quarterly operating margins swinging from ~8% to negative, and a meaningful portion of reported profit appears to come from interest income on IPO cash rather than core operations — a one-off tailwind that should fade as that cash is deployed or drawn down. Working-capital days have deteriorated sharply (18 to ~102 days), unusual for an OTA business model that should typically benefit from favorable working capital, and returns on capital remain low (mid-single-digit ROE/ROCE) against a rich ~118x earnings multiple and ~4.3x book value.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~118x trailing earnings with ROE only ~6-9% and a meaningful chunk of that profit non-operating (interest income), the multiple is effectively being paid against an even smaller true operating-profit base than headline numbers suggest, demanding sustained high-20s%-plus revenue growth with real margin expansion for years to justify today's price; given ROE is well under 20%, this does not qualify for the exceptional (>=25% growth, ROE>=20%) tier despite strong topline momentum, so I am setting a more moderate forward estimate that assumes growth moderates as the base scales and competition remains intense.
